newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 4.5/5.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 4.5/5.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 4.5/5.0 percent on Wednesday morning on sufficient liquidity and there was no apparent effect from the upcoming general elections on Thursday, dealers said.
Dealers said central bank supply of 591 billion rupiah seemed to keep the market flush despite the month-end factor.
Longer-term rates were also soft. One- and three-month money were at 12.50/12.75 and 13.5/13.75 percent, respectively.
Overnight swaps fell into the negative territory following the ample liquidity. They were last at -0.5/-0.2 points.
The central bank offered overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) at five percent, one-week at 6.5, two-week at 8.5 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The central bank will auction 100 billion rupiah in one-year SBIs (363 days) later on Wednesday. The last stop-off-rate of one-year SBIs were at 13.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 6.80 percent, compared with 9.16 percent on Monday.
Bond dealers said the market was still quiet, but some small trades were done.
"But people are rather reluctant to exchange orders. They prefer to keep a wait-and-see attitude," one bond dealer said.
